citation: Xia, Hengliang. 2025. Syntax of Classifiers and Measure Words in Three Chinese Languages. Proceedings of the 2025 Annual Conference of the Canadian Linguistic Association.
verified_claim: Distinguishes individual, kind, and individuating classifiers from container, group, partitive, and standard measure words; reports that Cantonese classifiers and measure words differ in preverbal bare, adjective, possessor, and Num-Adj profiles; shows Cantonese CL-N coordination and numeral-insertion behavior; proposes right-branching classifier and left-branching measure structures.
limitation: The Cantonese survey had seven valid Hong Kong or Guangzhou responses from fourteen recruits, and several judgements are gradient. The proposed branching analysis is one account; exact item typing and broader population scope need corroboration.

citation: Bond, Francis, and Joanna Ut-Seong Sio. 2024. A Construction-based Approach to Cantonese Classifiers. Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Head-Driven Phrase Structure Grammar, 60–75.
verified_claim: Distinguishes D-(X)-C-N, X-C-N, C-N, and N constructions; analyzes classifier phrases with and without an overt numeral separately and assigns no-numeral phrases semantic cardinality one.
limitation: The HPSG analysis does not provide an exhaustive classifier lexicon or a binary noun-pair compatibility table. Semantic cardinality one is not a hidden surface numeral.

citation: Cheng, Lisa Lai-Shen, and Rint Sybesma. 2014. The Syntactic Structure of Noun Phrases. In The Handbook of Chinese Linguistics, 248–274.
profile: Cantonese NP order, classifier phrases, and noun ellipsis
verified_claim: Documents [Dem (Num) CL N], bare CL-N, and classifier-supported noun ellipsis; argues that Cantonese CL-N does not require a covert numeral; treats classifier syntax and interpretation as variety-sensitive.
limitation: The chapter compares theories and does not assign every Cantonese unit word to one category or establish all noun-pair preferences.

citation: Matthews, Stephen, and Virginia Yip. Cantonese: A Comprehensive Grammar, multimedia Chapter 6, The noun phrase.
profile: Cantonese classifiers, measures, alternatives, and noun phrases
verified_claim: Separately illustrates sortal classifiers, measure and quantity expressions, alternative classifiers, demonstrative-classifier NPs, bare classifier NPs, and possessive or modifier-bearing classifier structures.
limitation: Edited examples provide strong occurrence and contrast evidence but not a complete source-ranked compatibility matrix or one mandatory theoretical taxonomy.

citation: Tse, Shek Kam, Hui Li, and Shing On Leung. 2007. The acquisition of Cantonese classifiers by preschool children in Hong Kong. Journal of Child Language 34(3):495–517.
locator: Abstract, typology, spontaneous-speech method, and classifier-production results
profile: Cantonese classifier inventory and child use
verified_claim: Finds a productive repertoire of 73 classifier types in spontaneous speech from 492 preschool children; reports broad use of general 個 and the influence of semantic, syntactic, cognitive, and contextual factors.
limitation: Child production can reveal acquisition and overextension but cannot by itself define adult preferred pairings or categorical ungrammaticality.

citation: Erbaugh, Mary S. 2013. Classifier choices in discourse across the seven main Chinese dialects. In Increased Empiricism: Recent Advances in Chinese Linguistics, 101–126.
profile: General, sortal, and alternative classifier choices
verified_claim: Reports that general classifiers dominate Cantonese discourse, sortals are comparatively infrequent, and synonymous or alternative sortals constitute a substantial portion of Cantonese sortal use.
limitation: Discourse frequency does not establish unrestricted substitution or the acceptability of a particular pair in every construction, register, or interpretation.

citation: Nagy, Naomi, and Samuel Lo. 2019. Classifier use in Heritage and Hong Kong Cantonese. Asia-Pacific Language Variation 5(1):84–108.
profile: Population and number effects on classifier choice
verified_claim: Finds similar strong preferences for general and mass classifiers in Hong Kong and Toronto heritage speech, classifier choice primarily governed by noun number, and increasing specialization of 個 toward singular nouns.
limitation: The abstract does not provide item-level sentence judgements. Population patterns cannot be converted directly into a lexical compatibility decision.

citation: Sybesma, Rint. 2017. Classifiers, Nominal. Encyclopedia of Chinese Language and Linguistics, vol. 1, 620–627.
locator: Section Sortals and measures; Cantonese and Mandarin examples
verified_claim: Defines sortal classifiers as naming an inherent semantic unit and measure expressions as creating a unit for counting or measuring; discusses functional and lexical properties in Cantonese and Mandarin.
limitation: The encyclopedia treatment is a broad theoretical overview and does not decide every polyfunctional Cantonese item or parser implementation.

citation: Her, One-Soon, and Chen-Tien Hsieh. 2010. On the Semantic Distinction between Classifiers and Measure Words in Chinese. Language and Linguistics 11(3):527–551.
locator: Refined semantic diagnostics and discussion of essential versus accidental properties
verified_claim: Argues that classifiers and measure words are semantically distinguishable and develops refined tests after rejecting simpler de-insertion and adjective-modification diagnostics as unreliable.
limitation: The principal data are not a Cantonese item inventory. The diagnostics inform category design but cannot replace Cantonese construction-specific evidence.

citation: Her, One-Soon. 2012. Distinguishing classifiers and measure words: A mathematical perspective and implications. Lingua 122(14):1668–1691.
profile: Semantic values of classifiers and measures
verified_claim: Proposes that both classifiers and measures act as multiplicands, but a classifier has value one while a measure word has a non-one measure value; reviews terminology and structural disagreements.
limitation: The formal semantic distinction is cross-Chinese and theory-dependent. It does not license hidden numerals or classify a Cantonese lexeme without construction-specific evidence.
